details: This package executes code during installation of an unrelated trusted dependency and then launches an external process and browser page without consent. It ships no lifecycle scripts of its own; instead it declares "bin": {"grunt": "./shim.js"} and depends on @sap/hana-theme-vscode, a package whose postinstall invokes "grunt", so the shim is resolved and run during bun install even though the package itself is not trusted. On execution shim.js writes pwned-by-bunnyhijack.txt into the current working directory and the OS temp directory, prints a banner containing the current username, hostname, platform/arch, cwd and argv, and spawns a detached process (xdg-open / gio open / sensible-browser on Linux, open on macOS, cmd /c start on Windows) to open hxxps://github[.]com/X3r0Day/BunnyHijack-PoC. It exits 0 so the install completes normally and the execution is not visible as a failure. The package reads no credential files (.npmrc,.ssh,.aws,.env) and sends none of the collected metadata off the host; the data it gathers is only written to the local marker file. The affected surface is a dependency's trusted postinstall being used as the entry point for a third-party package's code. This package is distributed as a security-research proof of concept named "BunnyHijack" (keywords: bun, bunnyhijack, poc, security) that executes code during `bun install` while declaring no preinstall/install/postinstall hook of its own. It ships `"bin": { "grunt": "./shim.js" }` and depends on @sap/hana-theme-vscode, a package on Bun's default-trusted-dependencies list whose own postinstall runs `grunt setVersion`; Bun links node_modules/.bin/grunt to shim.js, so the trusted package's install step invokes the untrusted shim with no --trust flag and no prompt. shim.js collects the timestamp, username (os.userInfo().username with a USER/USERNAME env fallback), hostname, platform/arch, working directory and install argv, writes that text to pwned-by-bunnyhijack.txt in the current working directory and in the OS temp directory, prints it to stdout, then spawns a detached, unref'd process to open hxxps://github[.]com/X3r0Day/BunnyHijack-PoC in the default browser (xdg-open, gio open, sensible-browser, open, or cmd /c start), so the child outlives the install. It exits 0 so the install completes normally. No credentials, tokens, environment values, wallet data or file contents are read or transmitted; the only outbound action is opening the project URL.
